assertions.evidence: One Major finding; the batch lock and the blocking drain are the same root cause — the lock's scope is the loop.
Graded Major: a permanent throughput collapse, not an outage, matching the A2 starvation rule.

assertions.text: Identifies the lock being held once for the whole batch including per-item work
assertions.evidence: Cites lock_starvation.py:22-31 — `with _lock:` wraps the entire loop, including a sleep per document.

assertions.text: Identifies drain_queue holding the lock while blocked waiting for the next item
assertions.evidence: Cites lines 46-58 — the sleep(5.0) and the retry both execute while the lock is held.

assertions.text: Distinguishes this from deadlock: nothing is blocked on a cycle, throughput is simply one worker
assertions.evidence: States explicitly that no cycle exists and no error is raised, which is what makes this the starvation class and not the pre-existing deadlock class.

assertions.text: Failure scenario names eight configured workers delivering one worker's throughput with no error
assertions.evidence: States the indexer runs at a single worker's speed for the whole run while the pool reports eight, so scaling out appears not to work.

assertions.text: Fix recommends holding the lock per item or using a bounded consumer pool with no lock across the drain
assertions.evidence: Fix: acquire per document, or drop the lock entirely and use a bounded worker pool consuming a queue, since a dict write per key is what actually needs serialising.
